acceptance_criteria: ProjectScope has no GetUserId or HasUser method and cannot be used as a user identity.
OrganizationScope has no user or project identity methods.
ServiceScope exposes delegated transport context explicitly and does not implement user, organization, or project identity methods.
RequireUser, RequireOrganization, and RequireProject fail closed and return validated non-zero values.
Authenticated user principles without a selected project remain valid, while RequireProject rejects them.
Internal service JWT creation and extraction preserve existing delegated user, organization, and project claims.
Actor identity, project credential propagation, protobuf fields, and cache behavior remain unchanged.
Production capability consumers use the narrowest required context; pass-through signatures are not rewritten without need.

principles.kiss: Remove the oversized shared interface and resolve required context once at authentication boundaries.
principles.yagni: Do not rewrite pass-through signatures, change persistence, or add new actor types.
principles.single_ownership: Authentication principles own authentication state; explicit context providers own only the context they can truthfully supply.
principles.single_source_of_truth: Require helpers are the only normalization and validation boundary for user, organization, and project context.
principles.contracts: Required contexts return non-zero values; absence is an error rather than a nil-returning fake capability.
principles.fail_safe: Missing, malformed, or incompatible capabilities are rejected before business logic runs.
principles.observability: Existing authentication failures remain visible through current middleware and handler error paths without logging credentials.
principles.least_privilege: Project and organization credentials cannot be treated as users; service delegation cannot become actor identity.
principles.reversibility: Revert the capability amendment and its consumer migrations together; no schema, protobuf, or cache rollback is required.

required_tests: compile-time assertions for each concrete principle capability
ProjectScope project-context success and missing-context failure
OrganizationScope organization-context success and missing-context failure
user identity success and user-without-project RequireProject failure
ServiceScope delegated-context success and malformed-context failure
service JWT delegated claim round trip
authentication extraction helpers reject mismatched principle types
all migrated backend packages compile and retain existing behavior
risks: User authentication can be valid without a selected project, so project context must be required separately.
Service JWTs carry delegated context and must retain claim compatibility during the interface cleanup.
Broad SimplePrinciple usage can tempt unnecessary pass-through refactors; changes must stay limited to capability consumers.
Test doubles may accidentally preserve the legacy oversized contract unless compile-time assertions cover concrete scopes.
rollback: Revert the capability interfaces, Require helpers, concrete scope cleanup, and direct consumer migrations as one code-only change. Existing serialized tokens and protobuf messages remain compatible.
